logLevel.//: Host.Results carries REQUEST telemetry and it is emitted at Information. Setting it to Error, as this file did until 2026-08-22, does not merely quieten it — it empties the AppRequests table completely. Nothing had ever appeared there. That is the table you need to answer 'did the timer fire' at Migration_Plan §6 step 7, so the scheduled-job gate was unobservable by construction.
logLevel.//1: Host.Aggregator was 'Trace'. The aggregator emits per-invocation rollups and Trace is the most verbose level there is; it was set for a diagnosis nobody recorded and then left on.
logLevel.//2: THE QUOTA KILLER. Azure.Core logs every SDK HTTP request and response at Information, and the host polls blob leases continuously — 76,125 messages and 39.3 MB in 24 hours, with Azure.Identity adding 4.4 MB. The workspace cap is 0.25 GB/day, so the platform's own chatter consumed most of it and ingestion went OverQuota at 01:33Z on 2026-08-22, silently discarding EVERY trace after that. Two investigations were blind for hours because a log line that was written correctly was thrown away at the door. Raising the cap would have paid for the noise instead of removing it.
